summary: A dashboard/agent that allows the crew members to record variables related to their health, and shows them in three categories, if their measurements surpass the expected range, they are notified to go and see a medic. It address the challenge by targeting the whole process of monitoring their health, and its experience, rather than a sole aspect of it. It's important because it allows the crew members to visualize properly their health in the long run. The environment chose for this project was the ISS.
details:
The project consists of a dashboard that allows crew members to log various health measurements. Based on these inputs, the system generates health graphs indicating whether their metrics fall within an acceptable range. If the results are abnormal and suggest a potential health issue, the user is urgently notified to consult a doctor. To improve usability, measurements can be entered via voice commands.

The intended impact focuses on making the health-tracking process more accessible. To develop this project, we used tools like Visual Studio Code and Antigravity for code debugging and troubleshooting , programming languages TypeScript, Python, and CSS, the React library, and CodeRabbit for continuous integration. Our project is creative because it offers an early version of an agent that process and monitors the health of the crew members, adding another layer to the verification of the health status. In developing this proposal, we considered several key factors. We evaluated the health-monitoring hardware most readily available to the crew to ensure practical usability. Additionally, we focused on environments with abundant data to ensure our approach is well-supported and justified.
